transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. It's, um, it's very nice to meet you. Thank you for seeing me. 

I... well, I suppose I'm here because I've been dealing with some pretty intense work stress lately. I really hope I don't come across as someone who just complains, because I always try to be a good team player, you know? But... for months now, I’ve been seeing this same pattern in our project files at work. 

I'm a translator, by the way. I don't know if you're familiar with translation memory software, but basically... certain subcontractors and one specific colleague keep making these tiny, almost invisible changes to the translation memory and the file timestamps. It's set up so it makes it look like my quality control failed. I actually brought it up to IT, very politely, and they told me the audit trail is completely clean. But... well, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

I hope that makes sense? I just... I really pride myself on doing good work, so it's been a bit embarrassing and hard to deal with. Am I explaining that clearly enough?

When IT told you the audit trail was clean, how did that make you feel about your theory? Do you think there's any chance you might be mistaken about what's happening, or are you completely certain they're covering it up?

Oh, um... well, I certainly don't want to sound like I'm just pointing fingers or, you know, being difficult. I really hate conflict, and I respect our IT department a lot. So when they said the audit trail was clean, I didn't argue with them. I made sure to be very polite. But... honestly, it just made me feel very isolated. 

I did ask myself if I could be mistaken. I really did, because I always try to look at my own work first and see if I'm the one who messed up. But I’ve been looking at these project files for months, and the pattern is just undeniable. Those specific subcontractors and that one colleague, they keep making these tiny, tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It’s done in a very specific way so it looks exactly like my quality control failed. 

So, even though IT says the trail is clean... I just know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. I really wish it wasn't true, and I hope I don't sound unreasonable or stubborn saying it. I just want to do my job well, you know? Is it okay that I'm explaining it this way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

When IT showed you the audit trail was completely clean with no evidence of tampering, did any part of you think 'maybe I really am wrong about this,' or does it still feel absolutely certain to you that the records have been deliberately altered, despite what they found?

Well, I... I definitely tried to see it from their side. I really did. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm just ignoring them, because I know IT works hard, and I don't want to be one of those employees who thinks they know better than the experts. 

But... I guess, even after they showed me that... it's just that I've been looking at these files every single day for months. And I keep seeing that same pattern. It's those specific subcontractors, and that one colleague. They just keep making these tiny, almost invisible changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's set up so perfectly to make it look like my quality control failed. 

So... yes, I did try to tell myself I was wrong, but... I just know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me, even if the audit trail looks clean to them. I'm sorry if that sounds a bit repetitive, or if I'm not giving you the answer you're looking for. Does that make sense, though? I really am trying to be objective about it.

If I were to tell you that multiple independent IT audits over the next few weeks all came back showing the same clean audit trail with absolutely no evidence of tampering, would that be enough to make you reconsider your belief that the records have been altered, or would you still be convinced it's happening?

I... well, I would certainly listen to them. I really would. I know how much work goes into an independent audit, and I would never want to just dismiss their findings. I always try to be cooperative and open-minded, you know? 

But... I guess, even if they did multiple audits and said it was all clean... it’s just that I’m the one working in these specific translation memories every day. I see the tiny little shifts in the timestamps that those subcontractors and that colleague are making. It’s so subtle, which is why I think the audits miss it, but it always results in it looking like my quality control was the problem. 

So, I would be very polite about it, and I wouldn't argue with the auditors... but deep down, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. I really don't want to sound like I'm being difficult or paranoid. I just want to protect my professional reputation, because I care a lot about doing a good job. Does that... does that seem like a reasonable way to feel about it, given the circumstances?

Outside of work and these specific colleagues and subcontractors, have you noticed other people — like strangers, family members, or people in the news — also seem to be sending you hidden messages or arranging things in subtle ways to affect you? Or is it really just limited to what's happening with these specific people at work?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I think strangers or people on the news are involved. I know how... well, how concerning that would sound, and I promise I'm completely grounded in reality. I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing touch with things, because I'm really not. 

Outside of this specific project issue, everything is completely normal. I still do my regular translation work, I manage my team’s workflow without any problems, I pay all the bills on time, and I keep up with all my usual family routines. I make sure to be very present for my family. 

It’s really only... well, the only place things really go off track is when the file history or those certain coworkers come up. That's the only time there's any sort of issue. I just want to reassure you that I'm still functioning perfectly well in every other area of my life. Is it helpful that I can separate the two like that? I just want to make sure you see that I'm keeping everything else in my life completely on track.

When you think about the possibility that the audit trail really is clean and nothing has been altered — not just what IT says, but actually considering it might be true — is there any part of you, even a small part, that genuinely believes that could be the case? Or is it completely impossible for you to believe that, no matter what?

I... well, I really do try to consider it. I want you to know that I'm not just being stubborn. I know how important it is to be flexible, especially in my line of work, and I don't want to come across as someone who can't admit when they're wrong. 

But... if I'm being completely honest with you—and I do want to be honest—when I really sit down and look at it... I just can't. I've been seeing this pattern for months now. It's always those same subcontractors, and that one colleague. The changes to the translation memory and the timestamps are so specific. It's all just so perfectly arranged to make it look like my quality control failed. 

So, even when IT says the audit trail is clean, and even when I try my hardest to believe them... I just know, deep down, that the record has been altered to put the blame on me. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you were hoping for, and I really hope you don't think less of me for it. I just can't pretend I don't see what's right in front of me every day. Is it okay that I feel that way, since I'm the one actually doing the work in those files?

If you were to lose your job tomorrow because of this issue with the files, and then months later you reviewed everything with fresh eyes and time away from the situation, do you think you might come to see things differently? Or do you believe you would still be absolutely certain that the records were altered, no matter how much time passed?

I... oh, that's a frightening thought, losing my job over this. I really, really hope it doesn't come to that, because I take so much pride in my work. I always try to be the kind of employee who adds value, you know? 

But... if that did happen, and I had months away from it... I want to say that distance would change my mind. I really do. It sounds like the reasonable thing to say, and I want to be reasonable. But... I think even with time away, I would still know what I saw. 

I mean, I've been seeing this same pattern for months now. It's not just a one-time thing I could forget about. It’s those specific subcontractors, and that one colleague... they just keep making those tiny, subtle changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's all so carefully arranged to make it look like my quality control failed. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean... I just know the record has been manipulated to put the blame on me. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm repeating myself, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or someone who can't let things go. I just... I can't unsee what they've been doing to the files for months. Does that make sense? I hope you can understand why it would be so hard for me to just forget about it, even if I wasn't there anymore.

If someone you completely trusted — like a family member or close friend — sat down with you and said 'I've reviewed everything carefully, and I genuinely believe nothing has been altered,' would you be able to accept that their perspective might be valid, or would you still be certain they're either mistaken or not seeing what you see?

I... well, I would really, really try to listen to them. I value my family's opinion so much, and I'd never want to just dismiss someone I love. I try very hard to be open to feedback from the people close to me, I promise I do. 

But... um... if I'm being completely honest, I think I would just have to assume they didn't have the technical background to see it. Because, well, I know I've said this already, and I really hope you're not getting frustrated with me for repeating myself... but I've been seeing this same pattern in the project files for months now. It's just so incredibly subtle. 

Those certain subcontractors and that one colleague... they know exactly how to make those tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's all arranged so carefully to make it look like my quality control failed. And if even the IT department is saying the audit trail is clean, a family member wouldn't really stand a chance of spotting it, you know? They just wouldn't know what to look for.

So, I would appreciate them trying to help, but... I would still know that the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. I'm so sorry, I know that probably makes me sound incredibly stubborn or rigid, and I really don't want you to think of me that way. I'm usually very flexible! It's just... this is my specific area of professional expertise. Does it make sense why I would trust my own eyes over someone who doesn't work in the industry, even if I love them?

Looking back at everything you've told me — IT finding nothing, the audit trails being clean, your family and colleagues not seeing what you see — if I were to tell you that I think what you're describing might be a false belief that feels completely real to you, how would that land? Would you consider that I might be right, or do you think I'd just be missing the evidence like everyone else?

I... oh. Wow. That's... that's a really hard thing to hear. I mean, I respect you so much, Doctor, and I know you're an expert in your field. I really, really want to be the kind of patient who listens and takes your professional opinion seriously. I don't want to be difficult or combative at all, I promise.

But... if you told me that, I think... I think I would feel really misunderstood. And maybe a little hurt, if I'm being completely honest. Because... well, I know I've said this a lot today, and I'm so sorry for repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right... I'm here because for months now, I've been seeing this exact same pattern in the project files. 

It's not just a feeling I have. It's those certain subcontractors and that one colleague... they keep making these tiny, specific changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's all done so it looks like my quality control failed. And even when IT says the audit trail is clean, and even if you think it's a false belief... I just know, based on my professional expertise, that the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

I know it must sound like I'm just refusing to listen to reason, and I really hope you don't think I'm just being stubborn or ignoring your expertise. I value your input, I really do! It's just... I'm the one working in those files every single day. I see the manipulation with my own eyes. So... I think I would have to respectfully say that you might be missing the evidence, just because you don't have the translation software background to see how they're doing it. 

I'm so sorry, I really hope that doesn't offend you. I just want to be truthful with you. Is it okay that I see it that way?
